sections.sectionSummaryBrief: On the first day of creation, heaven and earth and all their hosts were created ex nihilo, and this includes the creation of all later beings and even the substance of Adam, while the light created that day is a supernal light reserved for the future.

translations.translation: Now, on the first day of the six days of creation
(the twenty-fifth of Elul)
the heavens and the earth and all their hosts were created from nothing to something, as it is written,
"In the beginning, G-d created the heavens and the earth,"
meaning that the heavens and the earth and all their hosts
("the heavens" to include their offspring, and "the earth" to include its offspring)
were then created from nothing to something.
For even the creations that came into being on the subsequent days of the six days of creation—their revelation occurred then,
their formation and making—
but their creation from nothing to something was on the first day.
And also man,
regarding whom the quality of Rosh HaShanah is
(as above)
that on this day man was created,
it is written concerning him, "And the L-rd G-d formed the man of dust from the ground,"
and the dust from the ground
(from which the body of man was formed)
came into being on the first day.
And especially according to the known teaching
that the verse "In the beginning" etc. speaks of the coming into being of the physical heavens and earth, and also of the coming into being of Atzilus,
"In the beginning" is Chochmah,
"G-d" is Binah,
"the heavens" is Zeir Anpin, and "the earth" is Malchus.
And all this came into being on the first day.
And it is also brought in the Midrash on the verse "And there was evening and there was morning, one day,"
that what is said is "one day"
(and not "first day")
is because on it the Holy One, blessed be He, was alone in His world.
That is, the coming into being of the first day was in a manner that it was then seen and revealed that He is One in His world.
And this matter
(the Holy One, blessed be He, alone in His world)
was then from the aspect of above and from the aspect of, and as it was drawn below,
and the utterance that was said on the first day was "And G-d said, 'Let there be light,'"
through which the Children of Israel
(through their service)
can illuminate the entire world and reveal the innerness within it,
the Ein Sof that preceded creation and the tzimtzum,
and even to Awtsmoos and Essence,
which in the world as it is in itself
(even as it was created on the first day)
is in concealment.
And it can be said that this is what our sages, of blessed memory, said:
"The light that was created on the first day—the world was not worthy to use it,
and He set it aside for Himself,"
for this light is above the world,
and especially according to the explanation in many places
of the meaning
(and the greatness of the elevation)
of "He set it aside for Himself."

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: Although the world was created in its fullness in the six days, including the level of Gan Eden, the creation of man on Rosh HaShanah added a superiority by drawing down a light beyond the world's measures and limits.

translations.translation: Now, in addition to all the above elevations that were on the first day of the six days of creation,
it is known that in all six days of creation,
even on the sixth day of the six days of creation
(before the sin of the Tree of Knowledge),
the entirety of the world was on the level of Gan Eden.
For Gan Eden
(even as it is now)
is the most elevated level,
and certainly as it was then.
Nevertheless,
through the creation of man on Rosh HaShanah, an elevation was added to the world
[and even through the service of Adam the First, an elevation was added also to Gan Eden as it was then,
as it is written,
"And He placed him in Gan Eden to work it and guard it,"
to draw down Ein Sof into Gan Eden].
For although the world was created in its fullness,
and as it is written,
"These are the generations of the heavens and the earth when they were created," "generations" is written plene,
nevertheless, this perfection of the world is as the world is from the aspect of creation,
and as the precise language of the verse "These are the generations"
(plene)
etc. "when they were created,"
and likewise in the language of our sages, "The world was created in its fullness,"
the perfection of the world as it is from the aspect of creation
(from above)
is within measure and limitation.
And through the service of man, a light is drawn down that is above the measure and limitation of the world,
"These are the generations of Peretz"
"generations" plene,
meaning they break through
all the measures and limitations of the world,
even the measures and limitations of the world as it was on the first day of the six days of creation,
on which the Holy One, blessed be He, was alone in His world.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: Rosh HaShanah is specifically on the day Adam was created because its essence is drawing down the Essence of Ein Sof beyond relation to worlds, a power unique to Israel who are called "man."

translations.translation: And this is why Rosh HaShanah is specifically on the day Adam the First was created,
for the matter of Rosh HaShanah is the drawing down of this aspect
(as above in the explanation of "this day"),
namely,
the drawing down and revelation of the Essence of Ein Sof that is above the category of relation to worlds.
And "this day is the beginning of Your works,"
meaning that the revelation of this aspect is drawn down also into "Your works,"
for even in the world, which in itself is in the aspect of concealment, there will be in it a revelation of this aspect
(and even the aspect of "the deed"
(in the making)
"shall know that You have done it,"
as above).
Therefore, Rosh HaShanah is specifically on the day Adam the First was created,
for this power
(to draw down the revelation of the Essence of Ein Sof that is above the worlds,
and that this drawing down should be in the world)
is specifically in Israel,
"You are called 'man,'"
after Adam the First.
